title: Grafana -- dashboards, panels, alerting
exp:
Grafana turns metrics into visibility. The JD's near-real-time dashboard is likely Grafana.

Understanding Grafana -- dashboards, panels, alerting at a senior engineering level requires inspecting the runtime execution context, internal memory allocations, and network/storage constraints. In production systems operating under continuous high load, subtle architectural details determine whether a feature scales predictably or causes severe performance degradation.
pts: Data source: where metrics come from -- Prometheus, CloudWatch, Elasticsearch, PostgreSQL.
Panel types: Time series (over time), Stat (single value), Table, Gauge.
Dashboard variables ($source dropdown) filter all panels simultaneously -- avoids 50 dashboards for 50 sources.
Alerting: threshold on a panel; Grafana evaluates on schedule; notifies Slack/email/PagerDuty.

viz.note: Dashboard: Row 1 = Stat panels (records today, error rate, last run). Row 2 = Time series (records/hour, duration trend). Row 3 = Table (per-source status).

qa.q: What should a data pipeline Grafana dashboard include?
qa.a:
**Elevator Pitch:** Records ingested per run/source, job duration trend, error rate, EMR cluster cost/idle time, last successful run time per source. A Stat panel showing last run: 2 hours ago for an hourly job immediately surfaces a missed run.

**Under the Hood & Mechanics:** Cloud control plane APIs orchestrate virtualized hardware, networking (VPC/VNets), IAM policies, and auto-scaling groups.

**Production Failure Mode & Gotcha:** Overly permissive IAM roles (wildcard actions) or unmonitored resource limits lead to security breaches and unexpected cloud cost spikes.

**Senior Trade-Off Signal:** Serverless/managed services eliminate infrastructure maintenance but introduce cold starts and vendor lock-in.

**Elevator Pitch:** Dropdown filters at the top that filter all panels simultaneously. $source with values [Bloomberg, ICE] -- selecting one filters every panel. Avoids creating 50 identical dashboards. Interpolated into queries: rate(records{source='$source'}[5m]).
